items.title: Brain-Machine Interface With Virtual Reality and Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation for Upper Limb Rehabilitation After Stroke
items.summary: Stroke is a major cause of long-term disability, and many stroke survivors experience persistent difficulties moving and using their affected arm and hand. Improving upper limb function is an important goal of stroke rehabilitation. This study aims to investigate whether adding brain-machine interface (BMI) training to conventional rehabilitation improves upper limb motor recovery after stroke. The BMI system uses electroencephalography (EEG) to detect brain activity associated with imagined or attempted hand movements and provides visual feedback through virtual reality (VR).
